data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Scientific theories aim at truth, whereas hammers aim at utility; the teleology differs.","Nature can actively falsify theories, whereas wood does not actively break hammers to deceive.","Corroboration involves logical severity, while tool durability is often accidental."],"overturn_conditions":["If it is demonstrated that using the 'unbroken hammer' logically requires an assumption that the next strike will be like the previous ones.","If a superior method for action is found that does not rely on past survival data at all."],"shared_structure":["Selection of a tool based on past durability rather than predicted future performance.","Rejection of probabilistic forecasting in favor of robustness checking.","Action taken on the basis of 'least bad option' rather than 'most likely true'."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_004"],"transfer_claims":["Just as we use the hammer that hasn't broken yet without assuming it never will, we use the theory that hasn't failed yet without assuming it never will.","The rationality of the choice lies in the process of elimination, not in the prediction of success."]},"claim":"Preferring the better-corroborated theory is defensible on Popper's terms as a non-inductive, methodological decision to act on the theory that has withstood the most severe attempts at falsification, thereby maximizing verisimilitude without assigning probability; however, this stance costs us any logical guarantee that the future will resemble the past, forcing us to accept that our preference is rational only relative to the aim of truth, not predictive success.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If corroboration is shown to logically entail a probabilistic increase in truth likelihood, the non-inductive defense collapses.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If Popper's formal definition of verisimilitude is proven incoherent (as per Tich\u00fd/Miller) such that no comparison of truth-content is possible without probability, the justification fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the preference for action in novel domains cannot be distinguished from an implicit assumption of nature's uniformity, the charge of smuggling induction stands.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism is 'Critical Preferential Selection': agents treat corroboration reports not as inductive evidence of future truth (probability), but as a comparative metric of which theory has survived the most stringent tests. Action is guided by the methodological rule: 'In situations requiring action, choose the theory that is best tested,' because it aligns with the regulative idea of truth (verisimilitude). This avoids induction by refusing to infer 'will be true' from 'has been true,' instead inferring 'is the best available candidate for truth right now.'","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
